record.paper_title: Open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers
record.original_question: If Sigma is an r-minimizer for some compact target M, is Sigma the unique r-minimizer for its own closed r-neighborhood B_r(Sigma)?

evidence.quote: Question 1.5. Let Σ be an r-minimizer for some M. Is Σ the unique r-minimizer for B_r(Σ)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ and $r>0$. For a nonempty compact set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, define its closed $r$-neighborhood 
$$B_r(\Sigma)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d: \operatorname{dist}(x,\Sigma)\le r\}.$$
Given a compact set $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, a connected compact set $\Sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ is called an $r$-minimizer for $M$ if it has the minimal possible one-dimensional Hausdorff length $\mathcal{H}^1(\Sigma)$ among all connected compact sets $\Sigma'$ satisfying $M\subset B_r(\Sigma')$.

Suppose $\Sigma$ is an $r$-minimizer for some compact target set $M\subset\mathbb{R}^d$. Is $\Sigma$ necessarily the unique $r$-minimizer for the compact set $B_r(\Sigma)$ (i.e., taking the target equal to its own closed $r$-neighborhood)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent (2025) survey of open problems on Steiner trees and maximal distance minimizers. No published resolution was found in the literature search.
